reasoning.Student A:
This mechanism resembles a Deferred Acceptance (DA) / Gale-Shapley style school choice system, where students submit preference rankings and schools admit based on priorities. A key property of DA is strategy-proofness: truthful reporting of preferences is a dominant strategy, regardless of other applicants' preferences or the specific priority structure. Misrepresenting my preferences could only hurt me — it might cause me to be matched to a less preferred school or rejected from a school I could have gotten by ranking truthfully, since DA uses the submitted rankings to determine which schools you even get considered for at each round.

My true preference ordering is x > z > y > w. Given that I have priority 1 at y and w, priority 2 at x and z, there might be some temptation to think about strategic ordering based on competition (most others prefer y > x > w > z), but since DA is strategy-proof, the safest and optimal approach is to report my true preferences honestly. This maximizes my chances of getting matched to my most preferred feasible school given my priorities.

Thus, I will submit my true preference ranking.
